description: Reconstructing evolutionary history from molecular sequences: homology and models of sequence change, distance methods, parsimony, maximum likelihood, Bayesian inference, molecular clocks and the use of time-scaled phylogenies to track pathogen outbreaks. Practised by building and testing trees in browser-based simulators and on public alignments, with outbreak cases such as Ebola in West Africa, Lassa fever and cholera.
modelledOn: Yang, Molecular Evolution: A Statistical Approach
Lemey, Salemi and Vandamme, The Phylogenetic Handbook
outcomes: Explain mutation, selection, drift and homology and read rooted and unrooted trees, clades and branch lengths correctly.
Fit nucleotide and amino acid substitution models, compute corrected distances and build trees with UPGMA, neighbour joining and minimum evolution.
Score trees by parsimony and likelihood, implement Fitch and Felsenstein pruning algorithms and search tree space with heuristic rearrangements.
Run and diagnose Bayesian phylogenetic analyses, assess convergence and summarise posterior distributions of trees and parameters.
Estimate divergence times with strict and relaxed molecular clocks and test for temporal signal and selection with dN/dS.
Infer the origin, spread and growth of an outbreak from pathogen genomes with phylodynamic and phylogeographic methods and report the limits of the inference.

units.title: Evolution and homology
topics: Mutation, natural selection, genetic drift and gene flow; the neutral theory of molecular evolution
Homology versus similarity; orthology, paralogy and xenology; horizontal gene transfer in bacteria
Trees as hypotheses: rooted and unrooted, topology, branch lengths, clades, polytomies; Newick format
Rooting with outgroups and midpoint rooting; gene trees versus species trees
Selection in human populations: the sickle cell allele and balancing selection under malaria

units.title: Models of sequence evolution
topics: Substitution as a continuous-time Markov process: rate matrices and transition probabilities
Nucleotide models: Jukes-Cantor, Kimura two-parameter, HKY, GTR; base frequencies and transition bias
Rate heterogeneity among sites: gamma distribution and invariant sites
Amino acid and codon models; empirical matrices such as JTT, WAG and LG
Model selection with likelihood ratio tests, AIC and BIC

units.title: Distance-based tree building
topics: From alignments to distances: p-distance, saturation and model-corrected distances
UPGMA and the ultrametric assumption; when it fails
Neighbour joining derived and implemented step by step; minimum evolution and least squares
Additive and ultrametric metrics; the four-point condition
Speed versus accuracy: distance methods for very large datasets

units.title: Parsimony
topics: The principle of minimum change; informative and uninformative sites
The Fitch algorithm and weighted Sankoff parsimony; reconstructing ancestral states
Counting trees and searching tree space: exhaustive, branch and bound, heuristic searches
Long-branch attraction and statistical inconsistency of parsimony
Consensus trees: strict, majority-rule; measuring homoplasy with consistency indices

units.title: Maximum likelihood methods
topics: The likelihood of a tree; Felsenstein's pruning algorithm implemented
Optimising branch lengths and model parameters; tree rearrangements with NNI, SPR and TBR
Practical maximum likelihood with RAxML and IQ-TREE; partitioned analyses
Assessing support: non-parametric bootstrap, ultrafast bootstrap, SH-aLRT
Comparing trees statistically: KH, SH and AU tests; Robinson-Foulds distances

units.title: Bayesian phylogenetics
topics: Bayes' theorem for trees: priors on topology, branch lengths and parameters; posterior probabilities
Markov chain Monte Carlo: Metropolis-Hastings proposals, burn-in, mixing; coupled chains
Diagnosing runs: trace plots, effective sample size, convergence between independent runs
Summarising posteriors: maximum clade credibility trees, credible sets, posterior support compared with the bootstrap
Running MrBayes and BEAST; prior sensitivity and model averaging

units.title: Molecular clocks and selection
topics: The molecular clock hypothesis; testing it with likelihood ratio tests
Strict and relaxed clocks; calibration with fossils or sampling dates; tip-dating of rapidly evolving pathogens
Root-to-tip regression and temporal signal; estimating substitution rates and time to the most recent common ancestor
Detecting selection: synonymous and non-synonymous rates, dN/dS, site and branch models
Drug resistance and immune escape in Plasmodium falciparum as examples of positive selection

units.title: Tracking outbreaks with phylogenies
topics: Phylodynamics: coalescent and birth-death models; inferring effective population size and the reproduction number
Phylogeography: discrete trait and continuous diffusion models; reconstructing spread between districts and countries
Transmission trees versus phylogenies; within-host diversity and sampling bias
Real-time tools: Nextstrain, Nextclade and TreeTime; lineage nomenclature
Case studies: the 2014-2016 Ebola epidemic in West Africa, Lassa fever reservoirs and spillover, seventh-pandemic cholera lineages in Africa
Reporting phylogenetic evidence responsibly to outbreak response teams

units.title: Phylogenomics and project
topics: Phylogenomics: concatenation versus coalescent species-tree methods; incomplete lineage sorting
Recombination and reticulate evolution; networks and recombination detection
Reproducible phylogenetic workflows and archiving trees and alignments
Project: a dated phylogeny of a public pathogen dataset with an interpretation for public health

schedule.title: Evolution and reading trees
schedule.exercise: Explain why the sickle cell allele persists in malaria regions, then draw a tree from a Newick string and name its clades.

tasks.title: Parse five Newick strings into drawn trees, label clades and count tips, internal nodes and branch length totals
Root an unrooted tree with an outgroup and with the midpoint, then compare which clades change between the two rootings
Simulate genetic drift in populations of 20, 200 and 2000 for 100 generations and compare time to fixation of a neutral allele

schedule.title: Models of sequence evolution
schedule.exercise: Derive the Jukes-Cantor distance from the proportion of differing sites and explain why it exceeds the raw p-distance.

tasks.title: Compute Jukes-Cantor and Kimura two-parameter distances for 6 sequence pairs and compare them with raw p-distances
Exponentiate a rate matrix to get transition probabilities at several times and watch them converge to the base frequencies
Compare JC, HKY and GTR plus gamma on a given alignment using likelihood ratio tests, AIC and BIC, and justify the chosen model

schedule.title: Distance methods
schedule.exercise: Build a tree from a 5-taxon distance matrix by hand with UPGMA, then explain which assumption fails when rates differ between lineages.

tasks.title: Step through UPGMA on a 5-taxon distance matrix, record each merge and the updated matrix, and draw the final tree
Step through neighbour joining on a 6-taxon matrix, computing net divergences and Q values, then compare the tree with UPGMA's
Implement neighbour joining in code, test it on a matrix with unequal rates and check it recovers the true tree where UPGMA fails

schedule.title: Metrics and scaling distance methods
schedule.exercise: Test whether a 4-taxon matrix satisfies the four-point condition and use the result to choose the tree topology.

tasks.title: Check the four-point condition on three 4-taxon matrices and state which are additive and which are ultrametric
Measure how far a noisy distance matrix is from additivity by fitting a tree and reporting the residual squared error
Time neighbour joining on simulated datasets of 50, 200 and 800 taxa, fit the growth curve and estimate runtime for 10000 taxa

schedule.title: Parsimony
schedule.exercise: Count the number of unrooted binary trees for 4 to 10 taxa and explain why heuristic search is unavoidable.

tasks.title: Mark informative and uninformative sites in a 6-taxon alignment and score two candidate trees by minimum changes
Run the Fitch algorithm on a 7-taxon tree for three characters and reconstruct the ancestral state at every internal node
Simulate data from a tree with two long branches, show parsimony recovers the wrong tree, and test that a model-based method does not

schedule.title: Maximum likelihood
schedule.exercise: Compute the likelihood of a 3-taxon tree for one site by hand using Felsenstein's pruning recursion.

tasks.title: Step through pruning on a 4-taxon tree for one site, writing the conditional likelihood vector at each node and the final site likelihood
Implement Felsenstein's pruning for a JC69 model and compare tree log-likelihoods for the three topologies of a 4-taxon alignment
Optimise branch lengths and then apply NNI rearrangements to a starting tree until the likelihood stops improving, reporting each accepted move

schedule.title: Assessing support and comparing trees
schedule.exercise: Interpret bootstrap values of 55, 80 and 99 on three clades and write what each does and does not claim.

tasks.title: Compute Robinson-Foulds distances between five trees on the same 8 taxa and report the pair that disagrees most
Run 100 bootstrap replicates of a distance tree, tally clade frequencies and add the support values to the original tree
Compare two competing topologies with a paired site likelihood test, then explain why the test cannot favour the best tree without selection bias

schedule.title: Bayesian phylogenetics and MCMC
schedule.exercise: Explain in words how a Metropolis-Hastings accept or reject step moves a chain toward regions of high posterior probability.

tasks.title: Run Metropolis-Hastings on a one-parameter likelihood for 50 steps, recording each proposal, acceptance probability and decision
Sample the posterior of a substitution rate with MCMC, vary proposal width and compare acceptance rate and mixing
Run two independent chains on a 5-taxon problem, compute effective sample size and the split-frequency difference, and decide if they converged

schedule.title: Summarising posteriors and software
schedule.exercise: Compare a bootstrap proportion with a posterior probability for the same clade and explain why they differ.

tasks.title: Tally clade frequencies in 1000 sampled trees, report the majority-rule consensus and the 95 percent credible set of topologies
Pick the maximum clade credibility tree from a sample of 500 trees and annotate it with posterior probabilities and mean branch lengths
Rerun an analysis under three priors on branch lengths, compare the posterior for one clade and report sensitivity to the prior

schedule.title: Molecular clocks and selection
schedule.exercise: Estimate a substitution rate from a root-to-tip plot and explain the evidence for and against a strict clock.

tasks.title: Plot root-to-tip distance against sampling date for 30 isolates, fit a regression and read off the rate and root date
Calibrate a tree with two dated tips under strict and relaxed clocks and compare the estimated root ages and rate variation
Count synonymous and non-synonymous changes in an aligned gene, compute dN/dS per site and flag sites under positive selection in a drug target

schedule.title: Phylodynamics and phylogeography
schedule.exercise: Explain how branching times in a tree encode the growth rate of an outbreak and why uneven sampling can distort the inference.

tasks.title: Simulate a coalescent tree for constant and exponentially growing populations of 30 samples and compare their branch length patterns
Reconstruct the most likely location of ancestors on a tree of 25 isolates from 4 districts and count migration events between each pair
Simulate an outbreak and a biased sample, build the phylogeny and show how sampling changes the apparent source of introductions

schedule.title: Outbreak genomics in practice
schedule.exercise: Draft a half-page briefing for an outbreak response team stating what a tree shows, what it cannot show and how sure you are.

tasks.title: Place 5 new genomes onto a reference tree by nearest relative and report each sample's lineage label from its closest neighbour
Estimate the date of introduction and spread of an Ebola-like outbreak from a dated tree of 40 sequences and plot the lineage timeline
Brief an outbreak response team in a branching case, choose how to report uncertain tree evidence and be scored on accuracy and clarity

schedule.title: Phylogenomics, recombination and project
schedule.exercise: Present your dated phylogeny with a short public health interpretation and a list of the analysis files that make it reproducible.

tasks.title: Write a script that runs alignment, tree building and plotting end to end and records tool versions, then rerun it to verify identical output
Build gene trees for 5 loci and a concatenated tree, quantify their disagreements and say whether incomplete lineage sorting could explain them
Build a dated phylogeny of a public pathogen dataset with model choice, support values and root-to-tip checks, and write the public health interpretation
